subject: Follow-up: PT finding PT-2027-AUTH — token exposure and remediation timeline
messages:
From: PenTest Team <pentest@secureworks.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Alex Tang <alex.tang@greenfieldlogistics.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: PT delivery — token exposure (PT-2027-AUTH)

Hi Grace / Alex,

Attached is the consolidated penetration test report for the April engagement (PT-2027). The highest-severity finding is PT-2027-AUTH: a debug endpoint returned active bearer tokens and session cookies under a low-visibility path. Repro steps and PoC are in the report (attached: PT-2027-Report.pdf).

Immediate notes:
- Severity: HIGH (token exposure, potential account takeover)
- Affected components: auth-service v2.1 (internal path /debug/session)
- Suggested mitigation: disable debug endpoints, rotate active tokens/keys, add monitoring for access to debugging paths, and ensure short TTL for session cookies.

Please confirm receipt and who will own the remediation. We can schedule a 30-min call to walk through the PoC if helpful.

We will require proof-of-fix artifacts for closure: (1) a short remediation summary, (2) logs showing revoked/rotated keys or tokens, and (3) a test run demonstrating the debug path no longer returns credentials. ETA request: we typically ask for initial remediation evidence within 7 days.

Attachments: PT-2027-Report.pdf (34 pages, redacted PoC)

Best,
PenTest Team
SecureWorks Security Services

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: PenTest Team <pentest@secureworks.com>, Alex Tang <alex.tang@greenfieldlogistics.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PT delivery — token exposure (PT-2027-AUTH)

Thanks for the report and the clear PoC. Confirmed receipt.

Irene and Karthik — please take ownership of PT-2027-AUTH. Proposed triage/mitigation plan below:

1) Immediate (within 24 hours): disable or gate the /debug/* endpoints behind auth and block access from public routes. (owner: Irene)
2) Short-term (by 2027-04-28): rotate affected tokens and service keys, revoke long-lived sessions, and force re-auth for active users where feasible. (owner: Karthik)
3) Monitoring (by 2027-05-02): add alert for any access to debug endpoints and a short-term audit of token issuance patterns. (owner: Security Ops)

Deliverables we will provide to you for validation: remediation-plan-pt2027.xlsx (attached), screenshots of the disabled endpoint, and auth-service logs showing revocation (log extract). We will link artifacts in the shared drive and create JIRA INF-4821 to track the work.

Irene / Karthik — confirm if the dates above are feasible or propose adjustments. Alex, I will keep you updated daily until closure.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Security Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachment: remediation-plan-pt2027.xlsx

From: PenTest Team <pentest@secureworks.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Alex Tang <alex.tang@greenfieldlogistics.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PT delivery — token exposure (PT-2027-AUTH)

Thanks Grace — plan looks reasonable. A couple of clarifying items before we schedule verification:

- For rotation, please include a note of which secrets were rotated (service keys, signing keys, session secret). We need evidence that new tokens are signed with new keys.
- For the disabled endpoint, a simple curl showing HTTP 404/403 from an unauthenticated client is sufficient.
- If you can provide a short screen recording or timestamped log snippet showing token revocation, that expedites closure.

Requesting an initial evidence drop by 2027-04-26 so we can run a limited re-test before the full closure. If you need more time, please send revised ETAs.

We can take a follow-up 20-min call on Monday if helpful; ping the thread with preferred times.

Regards,
PenTest Team
SecureWorks

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: PenTest Team <pentest@secureworks.com>, Alex Tang <alex.tang@greenfieldlogistics.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PT delivery — token exposure (PT-2027-AUTH) — progress update

PenTest team / Alex — quick status update and artifacts for your triage: we completed the immediate mitigations today. Summary: 

- /debug/* endpoints disabled in production by feature flag; ingress rules updated to block public access. (evidence: evidence-rotation-screenshot.png)
- Rotated service signing key and revoked affected session tokens via auth-service API. Short log extract attached (auth-service-logs-20270425.txt) showing revocation events and new key ID (k-new-20270425).
- Created JIRA INF-4821 and uploaded remediation-plan-pt2027.xlsx and the drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cDE_pt2027_remediation

Requested next steps from us: we plan a controlled re-test window and will provide a consolidated evidence package for final verification by 2027-04-29. If you want an earlier re-test, we can open a 48-hour window starting 2027-04-26 with the artifacts already in place.

Let me know if the attached log snippets are sufficient for an interim verification; we can produce additional sanitized traces if needed.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Engineering Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachments: evidence-rotation-screenshot.png, auth-service-logs-20270425.txt
